cluster_summary: This cluster comprises 26 cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities caused by insufficient handling of user-supplied input. The common flaw is that user input is reflected or stored without proper HTML encoding, sanitization, or validation, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML/JavaScript. Fixes range from adding global input sanitization filters to per-field encoding, input validation, and removal of insecure features like JSONP.
guideline_text: Trace externally reachable requests, RPC messages, management calls, or background command triggers into privileged commands, administrative state changes, credential operations, or protected data access. Report code paths where caller identity is not established before the privileged action begins. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 8 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should require a validated session, principal, token, or authentication filter before any privileged effect.

mechanism.missing_guard: caller identity is not established before the privileged action begins
mechanism.name: missing authentication before privileged action
mechanism.sink_shape: privileged commands, administrative state changes, credential operations, or protected data access
mechanism.source_shape: externally reachable requests, RPC messages, management calls, or background command triggers
mechanism.typical_fix: require a validated session, principal, token, or authentication filter before any privileged effect

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add a global servlet filter that wraps the HttpServletRequest and sanitizes all parameter values using Jsoup.clean with a whitelist (e.g., Whitelist.basic()) before they reach controllers.
sub_patterns.name: Global servlet filter for input sanitization
sub_patterns.root_cause: The application lacked a centralized input sanitization mechanism; user-supplied parameters were processed and stored/rendered without any filtering of HTML tags or JavaScript, enabling XSS.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Apply input sanitization (e.g., Jsoup.clean with whitelist, OWASP HTML sanitizer, HTML tag stripping) to those fields before persisting them in the database or using them in further processing.
sub_patterns.name: Missing input sanitization on specific fields
sub_patterns.root_cause: Specific input fields (e.g., solutionId, nickname, firstName, lastName, group name) were stored without any sanitization or encoding, assuming they were safe.

sub_patterns.name: Missing HTML escaping and input sanitization in web endpoints
